sentences.en: For most Americans, the government's monthly jobs number was a pretty dull statistic.

sentences.en: Until a few days ago, when President Trump angrily fired the person responsible for producing it.
sentences.zh: 直到几天前，特朗普总统愤怒地解雇了负责发布该数据的人。

sentences.en: The commissioner of the Bureau of Labor Statistics.
sentences.zh: 也就是劳工统计局局长。

sentences.en: Now, from Washington to Wall Street, everyone's wondering whether you can still trust federal statistics if the president is willing to just get rid of people who give him facts
sentences.zh: 现在，从华盛顿到华尔街，每个人都在怀疑，如果总统可以随意开除那些提供他不喜欢的真相的人，那么联邦统计数据是否还值得信任。

sentences.en: he doesn't like.

sentences.en: I mean, you have made a career of labor numbers, and this time, we didn't just get job numbers.

sentences.en: There was extreme drama around these job numbers.

sentences.en: So, every month, the Bureau of Labor Statistics, or the BLS, puts out this big report on jobs, hiring, employment, unemployment from the previous month.
sentences.zh: 每个月，劳工统计局（BLS）都会发布一份关于上个月就业、招聘、雇佣和失业情况的大型报告。

sentences.en: And it is my Super Bowl, 12 times a year.
sentences.zh: 这确实是我的“超级碗”，一年有12次。

sentences.en: Lucky for you.
sentences.zh: 你真幸运。

sentences.en: It's my Super Bowl.
sentences.zh: 这是我的“超级碗”。

sentences.en: It's the Super Bowl for a lot of econ nerds around the country.
sentences.zh: 对于全国许多经济学书呆子来说，这就是他们的“超级碗”。

sentences.en: And that's because this is, in some ways, the most important single number or single set of numbers that we get about the economy each month.
sentences.zh: 这是因为在某种程度上，这是我们每月获得的关于经济的最重要的单一数字或单一数据组。

sentences.en: It matters to regular people, right?

sentences.en: This is about whether people have jobs and can find jobs.
sentences.zh: 这关乎人们是否有工作，能否找到工作。

sentences.en: It's important to policymakers at the Federal Reserve who are trying to decide whether they should raise or lower interest rates.
sentences.zh: 这对美联储的决策者也很重要，他们正试图决定是否应该加息或降息。

sentences.en: It's a hugely important political number that tells us, as well as any other set of numbers, whether the president is succeeding or failing in his management of the economy.
sentences.zh: 这是一个极其重要的政治数字，它和任何其他数据组一样，能告诉我们总统在经济管理上是成功还是失败。

sentences.en: And so, this is a set of numbers that we all sort of drill down on the moment they come out.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一组我们所有人都会在发布那一刻仔细钻研的数据。

sentences.en: They hit the website at 8.30, and we're all sort of frantically refreshing to see what these numbers show.
sentences.zh: 它们在8点半发布到网站上，我们都在疯狂刷新页面，看看这些数字显示了什么。

sentences.en: Which is not great.

sentences.en: Hmm.

sentences.en: So, we thought we had added around 150,000 jobs a month in May and in June, which would have been solid numbers.

sentences.en: We had reacted to them and said, these are great numbers.

sentences.en: Right.

sentences.en: Those got revised down to more like 15,000 jobs in each of those two months.

sentences.zh: 所以，突然之间，我们对劳动力市场的看法——这个曾经稳步前进、富有韧性、

sentences.en: And if there are big changes and big revisions, we expect more big revisions for the jobs data in September, for example, that we want to know why.

sentences.en: And how much money were they paid?
sentences.zh: 但我们正试图衡量一个拥有1.6亿雇员、价值30万亿美元的巨大经济体。

sentences.en: And those numbers get aggregated together and added up to come up with a jobs number.
sentences.zh: 试图整理这些数字、填补缺失的空白需要做很多工作。

sentences.en: But we're trying to measure an enormous $30 trillion economy with 160 million employees.
sentences.zh: 而我们所有人如此关注的那个最初发布的数字只是一个估算值。

sentences.en: There's a lot that goes into trying to tabulate those numbers, to try to fill in the missing blanks.
sentences.zh: 这是一个初步估算。

sentences.en: And that first number that comes out that we all pay so much attention to is an estimate.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: It's a preliminary estimate.
sentences.zh: 随着我们获得更完整的数据，我们会随着时间的推移对其进行更新。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And we update it over time as we get more complete numbers.
sentences.zh: 明白。

sentences.en: And sometimes those updates can be pretty substantial.
sentences.zh: 有时这些更新可能会非常重大。

sentences.en: These are the revisions, right?
sentences.zh: 这些是修正值，对吧？

sentences.en: These are the revisions.
sentences.zh: 这些就是修正值。

sentences.en: How should we think about those, Ben?
sentences.zh: 本，我们该如何看待这些修正值呢？

sentences.en: Because I'm just wondering, for people who are not intimately familiar with this data set,
sentences.zh: 因为我只是在想，对于那些不太熟悉这套数据集的人来说，

sentences.en: it may seem odd that there are really dramatic changes to data that is, I mean, you've been saying, so important.
sentences.zh: 数据出现如此剧烈的变化可能会显得很奇怪，毕竟你一直说这些数据非常重要。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's completely understandable.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这完全可以理解。

sentences.en: I think if you hear we thought there were 150,000 jobs added in June, and now we say there are 15,000 jobs added, that you say, well, what good is any of this anyway?
sentences.zh: 我想如果你听到我们之前认为六月份增加了15万个就业岗位，而现在却说只增加了1.5万个，你肯定会问，这些数据到底有什么用？

sentences.en: But it's important to understand that there are some reasons for these big revisions.
sentences.zh: 但重要的是要明白，这些大幅修正是有原因的。

sentences.en: Like what?
sentences.zh: 比如什么原因？

sentences.en: As I said, big survey, not everybody responds to the survey right away.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，这是一项大型调查，并非每个人都能立即回复。

sentences.en: Over the course of the next two months, more data becomes available, and so we get a more complete read.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的两个月里，会有更多数据可用，因此我们能得到更完整的结果。

sentences.en: And in normal times, this really works pretty well.
sentences.zh: 在正常时期，这种方法效果相当不错。

sentences.en: You miss a little bit up one month.
sentences.zh: 某个月可能会稍微高估一点。

sentences.en: You miss a little bit down one month.
sentences.zh: 某个月可能会稍微低估一点。

sentences.en: But over time, it pretty much smooths out.
sentences.zh: 但随着时间推移，数据基本会趋于平稳。

sentences.en: The trick is that at times when the economy is changing a lot, it can be difficult to get a clear read, right?
sentences.zh: 诀窍在于，当经济发生剧烈变化时，很难获得清晰的解读，对吧？

sentences.en: It may be that those people who didn't respond to the survey the first time don't look like the people who did respond.
sentences.zh: 可能那些第一次没有回复调查的人，与那些回复了的人情况并不一样。

sentences.en: Maybe the reason they didn't respond to the survey was that they were scrambling to keep the lights on, and so they were cutting jobs, and they can't even deal with the survey.
sentences.zh: 也许他们没有回复调查的原因是他们正忙于维持经营，甚至在裁员，根本无暇顾及调查。

sentences.en: Maybe those businesses shut down altogether, and the reason they didn't respond was not that they hadn't gotten around to it yet, but that they don't exist anymore.
sentences.zh: 也许那些企业已经彻底倒闭了，他们没回复不是因为还没来得及，而是因为他们已经不存在了。

sentences.en: And so once we get all of the information in, we learn, ooh, actually, we did not add as many jobs as we thought.
sentences.zh: 所以一旦我们收集到所有信息，就会发现，哦，实际上我们增加的就业岗位并没有预想的那么多。

sentences.en: And so we know that we have a harder time picking up what's happening at turning points of the
sentences.zh: 因此我们知道，在经济转折点时，我们更难捕捉到实际情况，

sentences.en: economy, which is part of why when these numbers came out on Friday, a lot of people said, uh-oh, maybe this suggests that we are at one of these turning points.
sentences.zh: 这也是为什么周五这些数据公布时，很多人说，糟了，这可能暗示我们正处于转折点之一。

sentences.en: Maybe this suggests that the economy is really taking a turn for the worse.
sentences.zh: 也许这暗示着经济真的在恶化。

sentences.en: So you have these Trump aides pointing to the revision saying, look, why are these so big?
sentences.zh: 所以特朗普的助手们指着修正值说，看，为什么这些修正幅度这么大？

sentences.en: And what you're saying is one of the reasons they may be so big is that things have just been really volatile recently.
sentences.zh: 而你的意思是，修正幅度之所以这么大，原因之一是最近的情况确实非常不稳定。

sentences.en: I assume we've seen things that are creating a lot of noise.
sentences.zh: 我想我们已经看到了很多制造噪音的因素。

sentences.en: They're creating a lot of noise, and anything that creates a lot of noise just makes it more difficult to measure the economy in real time.
sentences.zh: 它们制造了大量噪音，而任何制造大量噪音的事物都会使实时衡量经济变得更加困难。

sentences.en: But just to be clear, is there anything to suggest that these numbers themselves are wrong?
sentences.zh: 但为了明确起见，有什么迹象表明这些数字本身是错误的吗？

sentences.en: It depends what you mean by wrong.
sentences.zh: 这取决于你所说的“错误”是什么意思。

sentences.en: If what you mean is that these numbers are not a perfect reflection of the actual number of jobs in this country, then yes, because all of these numbers are wrong when they first
sentences.zh: 如果你是指这些数字不能完美反映该国实际的就业人数，那么是的，因为所有这些数字在刚发布时都是错误的，

sentences.en: come out.
sentences.zh: 它们只是估算值。

sentences.en: They're estimates.
sentences.zh: 它们只是估算值。

sentences.en: But they are the best estimates using the best methods that we have available to us.
sentences.zh: 但它们是我们利用现有最佳方法得出的最佳估算值。

sentences.en: But remember, the president didn't just say wrong.
sentences.zh: 但请记住，总统不仅仅是说“错误”。

sentences.en: He said rigged.
sentences.zh: 他说的是“操纵”。

sentences.en: He said these numbers were rigged out of political bias against him.
sentences.zh: 他说这些数字是出于对他个人的政治偏见而被操纵的。

sentences.en: And there's absolutely no evidence for that.
sentences.zh: 而这完全没有任何证据。

sentences.en: But I think that that suggestion by the president is what has so many people so alarmed right now.
sentences.zh: 但我认为总统的这种暗示正是让现在这么多人感到恐慌的原因。

sentences.en: So we'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Wena Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是 Wena Liu。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我负责编写《纽约时报》游戏中的《Connections》谜题。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我还喜欢尝试捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是 Sam Mazursky，我每天负责制作《Spelling Bee》和《Letterboxd》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做“联觉”的特质。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你们刚才听到的人那样的人制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com/games 立即开始游戏。

sentences.en: So you said, Ben, that this has a lot of people alarmed.
sentences.zh: 本，你刚才说这让很多人感到恐慌。

sentences.en: Just explain to me why this matters so much to so many people.
sentences.zh: 请向我解释一下，为什么这对这么多人来说如此重要。

sentences.en: It matters because it gets to the real core of how we understand our economy and to the credibility of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这之所以重要，是因为它触及了我们理解经济的核心，以及美国政府的信誉问题。

sentences.en: government.
sentences.zh: 我想我们在历史上已经看到过当这种信任被侵蚀时会发生什么。

sentences.en: And I think we have seen in history what happens when that confidence is eroded.
sentences.zh: 虽然不是发生在这个国家，但在其他国家确实发生过。

sentences.en: Not so much in this country, but in other countries.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为这方面的典型例子是阿根廷，在本世纪初，他们解雇了负责发布通胀数据的人员，

sentences.en: You know, the canonical example of this, I think, is Argentina, where in the earlier part of this century, they fired the people responsible for putting out their inflation numbers
sentences.zh: 因为当时的通胀数据比他们预期的要高，这在当下听起来确实有点耳熟。

sentences.en: when the inflation numbers were higher than they wanted, which certainly sounds a little bit familiar right in this moment.
sentences.zh: 然后他们继续发布低通胀数据，这些数据对任何人来说都不可信。

sentences.en: And then kept putting out low inflation numbers that were just not credible to anyone.
sentences.zh: 它们在国内对任何人来说都不可信，在国外也同样不可信，

sentences.en: They were not credible to anyone in the country and they were not credible to anybody outside of the country
sentences.zh: 以至于国际社会基本上完全停止关注阿根廷的官方通胀数据了。

sentences.en: to the point that the international community basically stopped paying any attention to Argentina's official inflation numbers altogether.
sentences.zh: 这在阿根廷产生了真实的后果。

sentences.en: And that had real consequences in Argentina.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们当时在国际上借款，投资者基本上开始要求更高的溢价才愿意借钱给他们，

sentences.en: You know, they were borrowing money internationally and investors basically started charging a higher premium to lend them money
sentences.zh: 因为他们不信任通胀数据，也不信任政府。

sentences.en: because they didn't trust the inflation numbers and they didn't trust the government.
sentences.zh: 这导致了阿根廷严重的债务危机和违约。

sentences.en: And that contributed to a really crippling debt crisis and default in Argentina.
sentences.zh: 投资者基本上是在说，我们不相信你们能掌控局面。

sentences.en: Investors were basically saying, we don't trust that you have a handle on this.
sentences.zh: 没有一个我们可以真正参考的标尺来判断它是真实的。

sentences.en: There's no yardstick that we can really point to and know that it's real.
sentences.zh: 如果你向银行谎报收入，他们很可能不会给你很好的抵押贷款利率。

sentences.en: If you lie to your bank about your income, they're probably not going to give you a very good rate on your mortgage.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是我们在这里讨论的问题。

sentences.en: And that's basically what we're talking about here.
sentences.zh: 我们在希腊也看到了这种情况，政府多年来一直在赤字数据上弄虚作假，试图达到欧盟的某些目标，

sentences.en: We saw this in Greece as well, where the government fudged the numbers on their deficit for years to try to meet certain European Union targets,
sentences.zh: 这最终导致了那里的大规模债务危机。

sentences.en: which eventually led to a massive debt crisis there.
sentences.zh: 更糟糕的是，当他们聘请一位经济学家来管理统计机构以清理这些问题，而他说了实话时，

sentences.en: And what's worse, when they brought in an economist to run their statistical agency to kind of clean things up, and he told the truth about what the numbers were,
sentences.zh: 这触怒了当地的当局。

sentences.en: that ran afoul of the authorities there.
sentences.zh: 他们对他进行了刑事起诉。

sentences.en: And they criminally prosecuted him.
sentences.zh: 多年来，他一直在为这些案件抗争。

sentences.en: For years, he's still fighting those cases.
sentences.zh: 好的，本，你给了我们这两个例子，在这两个案例中，政府似乎很明显是在故意掩盖非常糟糕的经济现实。

sentences.en: Okay, you've given us these two examples, Ben, where it seems pretty clear that the governments in these two cases were deliberately obscuring a very bad economic reality.
sentences.zh: 但这种情况正在这里发生吗？

sentences.en: But is that happening here?
sentences.zh: 我们是否正朝着那个方向发展？

sentences.en: Like, is that what we're headed for?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这肯定不是我们现在的处境。

sentences.en: Well, so it's certainly not where we are now.
sentences.zh: 目前，我们所有的证据都表明，政府迄今为止发布的数据一如既往地值得信赖。

sentences.en: Now, all of our evidence is that the data that's been put out by the administration so far is as trustworthy as ever.
sentences.zh: 而现在负责劳工统计局（BLS）的人，是在局长被解职后代理职位的，他是一位资深的公务员。

sentences.en: And the person who's in charge of the BLS now, who took over on an acting basis after the commissioner was pushed out, he's a longtime civil servant.
sentences.zh: 他受到广泛且高度的评价。

sentences.en: He's very widely and well-regarded.
sentences.zh: 我不认为有任何迹象表明他会造假。

sentences.en: I don't think there's any suggestion that he would cook the books.
sentences.zh: 正如我们之前讨论的那样，这些数字实际上是由幕后的一大批公务员制作的，

sentences.en: And as we discussed before, right, the numbers are actually produced by this legion of civil servants beneath the surface,
sentences.zh: 也没有理由认为他们中的任何人会改变做事方式。

sentences.en: and there's no reason to think that any of them are going to change the way they do things either.
sentences.zh: 我认为令人担忧的是总统将任命一位新局长。

sentences.en: I think the concern is the president's going to name a new commissioner.
sentences.zh: 我们还不知道那个人是谁。

sentences.en: We don't know who that is yet.
sentences.zh: 也许会是一位非常有资格的人。

sentences.en: Maybe it will be somebody extremely qualified.
sentences.zh: 我得说，在特朗普第一任期内管理劳工统计局的人，一个叫 Bill Beach 的人，受到了广泛的尊重。

sentences.en: I will say that the person who ran the BLS in Trump's first term, a man named Bill Beach, was very widely regarded.
sentences.zh: 他已经公开谴责了这次解雇事件。

sentences.en: He has come out and condemned this firing.
sentences.zh: 但如果再次任命像他这样的人，我认为很多担忧会在一定程度上得到缓解。

sentences.en: But if somebody like him is put into place again, I think that a lot of these concerns will be mitigated to a degree.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这种想法现在已经存在了，人们担心的是，如果总统可以因为某人发布了他不喜欢的数字而解雇他，也许他还会解雇下一个人，

sentences.en: But I think the idea is out there now, and the concern is that if the president can fire one person for putting out numbers he doesn't like, maybe he fires another,
sentences.zh: 也许我们最终会陷入一种局面，这种情况会一直持续，直到他得到他喜欢的数字为止。

sentences.en: and maybe we end up in a situation where this keeps going until he gets numbers that he likes.
sentences.zh: 你基本上是说，无论如何，

sentences.en: You're saying basically that either way,
sentences.zh: 特朗普至少已经给人留下了这样的印象：如果你提供的数据不是他想看到的，他就会解雇你。

sentences.en: Trump has at the very least created the impression that he's willing to fire you if you produce numbers that are not what he wants to see.
sentences.zh: 我想我的问题是，我们真的应该期待他任命一个上任后就大幅向上修正数据的人吗？

sentences.en: I guess my question has been, should we really expect, you know, him to appoint somebody who comes in and then just kind of revises the numbers way upward?
sentences.zh: 那难道不会非常明显吗？

sentences.en: Like, wouldn't that be extremely obvious?
sentences.zh: 没人会相信这一点。

sentences.en: No one would trust that.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，看，理论上，他可以任命某个长期效忠者上任，然后那个人就说，从现在开始，我们每月增加25万个就业岗位。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, look, in theory, right, he could appoint some longtime loyalist to come in who just says, like, from now on, we added 250,000 jobs a month.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这有点像苏联式的做法，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, something sort of very Soviet, right?
sentences.zh: 我不认为这很可能发生。

sentences.en: And I don't think that's likely.
sentences.zh: 那会非常明显。

sentences.en: It would be extremely obvious.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 我没有在预测任何事情。

sentences.en: I'm not predicting anything.
sentences.zh: 你和我六周后可能还会坐在这里讨论那个场景，但我并不是在预测它。

sentences.en: You and I may be sitting here in six weeks' time talking about that scenario, but I'm not predicting that.
sentences.zh: 你还没到那一步。

sentences.en: You're not there yet.
sentences.zh: 我还没到那一步。

sentences.en: I'm not there.
sentences.zh: 不过我认为还有另一种版本，虽然稍微温和一些，但我认为在某些方面同样令人担忧。

sentences.en: I think there's another version of this, though, that is a little bit softer, but I think is in some ways just as concerning.
sentences.zh: 总统带来的人可能不是明显的唯唯诺诺者，但他们不维护这些机构的传统，

sentences.en: Where the president brings in somebody who maybe isn't an obvious yes man, but who doesn't uphold the traditions of these agencies,
sentences.zh: 这会导致员工士气下降，人员流动率增加。

sentences.en: and that that leads over time to a diminishment of staff morale, to increase turnover.
sentences.zh: 你知道，很多在这些地方工作的人已经工作很长时间了。

sentences.en: You know, a lot of these people who work in these places have been there for a long time.
sentences.zh: 他们的收入未必很高。

sentences.en: They don't necessarily make that much money.
sentences.zh: 我们已经看到了很多人员流失，这只会侵蚀专业知识，并最终影响这些数字的质量，

sentences.en: We've already seen a lot of turnover and that it just eats away at the expertise and ultimately at the quality of these numbers
sentences.zh: 以至于人们不再相信它们是衡量经济的有用指标了。

sentences.en: to a point that people just sort of lose faith in them as being useful gauges of the economy anymore.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，没有人会忽略这样一个事实：这是一种在总统领导下，联邦政府许多部门都在上演的模式。

sentences.en: And, you know, I don't think it's lost on anybody that this is a pattern that has played out in a lot of places within the federal government under this president.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们在科学、卫生和环保署（EPA）都看到了这种情况，虽然在统计机构中还没有以这种方式看到，

sentences.en: You know, we've seen this in the sciences and in health, in the EPA, and we haven't seen that in this way at the statistical agencies yet,
sentences.zh: 但想象它发生并不难。

sentences.en: but it doesn't take that much to imagine it happening.
sentences.zh: 好的，本，我们一直在谈论关于这些数据的争论，但我现在想回到数据本身。

sentences.en: Okay, Ben, we've been talking about the rhetoric, about the battle over this data, but I want to now just turn back to the data itself.
sentences.zh: 请给我一个非常清晰的分析，说明这些数字反映了我们目前的经济状况。

sentences.en: Give me a really clear-eyed analysis of what these numbers say about where we are economically right now.
sentences.zh: 给我们指明方向。

sentences.en: Give us our bearings.
sentences.zh: 我想你在本集开头提到了我们上次的谈话，我们谈到了现在是特朗普的经济，

sentences.en: So I think you alluded at the beginning of the episode here, right, to the last time we talked and we talked about how this was Trump's economy now,
sentences.zh: 但并没有太多证据表明这些政策（关税、移民、不确定性等）正在以显著方式损害经济。

sentences.en: but there really wasn't much evidence that these policies, tariffs and immigration and uncertainty and all of this, were really hurting the economy in a significant way.
sentences.zh: 我想我们不能再那样说了。

sentences.en: I think we can't say that anymore.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是因为就业数据。

sentences.en: That's not just because of the jobs numbers.
sentences.zh: 这也是因为我们上周收到的一些关于消费者支出和商业投资的数据。

sentences.en: It's also because of some of the numbers that we got on consumer spending last week, that we've gotten on business investment.
sentences.zh: 我们已经开始看到一些迹象，表明总统采取的各种政策开始侵蚀经济的增长势头。

sentences.en: We've started to see some signs that various policies that the president has adopted are starting to sort of eat away at the momentum in the economy.
sentences.zh: 但我们仍然处于一个没有看到经济出现巨大鸿沟的阶段。

sentences.en: But we also still are in a place where we are not seeing sort of deep chasms forming in the economy.
sentences.zh: 失业率仍然很低。

sentences.en: The unemployment rate is still low.
sentences.zh: 我们没有陷入衰退，我交谈过的预测者中很少有人认为我们即将陷入衰退。

sentences.en: We're not in a recession, and very few forecasters that I talk to think that we're headed for one anytime imminently.
sentences.zh: 因此，尽管我们上周得到的数据表明经济状况比我们预想的要差，

sentences.en: And so although the data that we got last week suggests that the economy is in worse shape than we had known going into it,
sentences.zh: 但我不知道这是否改变了一个基本事实，即经济表现出了相当的韧性，但也面临着许多挑战。

sentences.en: I don't know that it changes the sort of fundamental story of an economy that has proved pretty resilient but faces a lot of challenges.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 这太有趣了，老实说，考虑到我们刚才花了这么多时间讨论特朗普对这些数字的强烈反弹，这确实令人惊讶。

sentences.en: That is so interesting and honestly quite surprising given that we've just spent all this time talking about the intense backlash from Trump that these numbers elicited.
sentences.zh: 是的，在某些方面，这就是总统周五的反应如此令人惊讶的原因。

sentences.en: Yeah, in some ways this is why the president's reaction on Friday was so surprising.
sentences.zh: 除了他所作所为带来的震惊之外，这似乎与新闻的实际情况不成比例。

sentences.en: Beyond the shock of what he was doing, it just seemed sort of disproportionate to the actual reality of the news.
sentences.zh: 让我们从这些数字开始，因为我们得到的数字低于彭博社经济调查的所有预期。

sentences.en: Let's just start with these numbers because the figure that we got, that was below all estimates in the Bloomberg survey of economy.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在报告发布后的最初几个小时里——

sentences.en: You know, in the initial hours after the report came out—
sentences.zh: 我们确实看到了就业增长，而且是针对美国本土出生的劳动力。

sentences.en: We've seen positive job growth, for sure, and they've been for the American workforce, native-born workers.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，考虑到所有——

sentences.en: I mean, with all—
sentences.zh: 总统的许多助手都在电视上，做着他们通常做的事情。

sentences.en: A lot of the president's aides were, you know, out on TV, and they were doing their usual thing.
sentences.zh: 他们正在进行通常的宣传，说这些数字其实并没有那么糟糕。

sentences.en: They were doing their usual sort of spin about how these numbers weren't really so bad.
sentences.zh: 你知道，很多数据是在那项宏伟的法案之前得出的。

sentences.en: You know, a lot of that data comes pre-one big beautiful bill.
sentences.zh: 现在我们有了那项宏伟的法案，并且对税收的去向有了更好的了解，我认为我们会看到更多投资。

sentences.en: Now that we have one big beautiful bill and we have a better sense of where the taxes are going, I think we're going to see a much—we're going to see more investment.
sentences.zh: 就像你说的，这是一个相对较小的数字，所以我并不觉得它非常糟糕。

sentences.en: And like you said, it's a relatively small number, so I don't—I don't read terrible.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，他们给出的理由相当充分。

sentences.en: And, you know, they were making a pretty good case.
sentences.zh: 这些数字中确实有很多疲软之处。

sentences.en: There was certainly a lot of softness in these numbers.
sentences.zh: 这一点是无法回避的。

sentences.en: There's no getting around that.
sentences.zh: 这些不是白宫所希望看到的数字，但是——

sentences.en: These were not the numbers the White House was hoping for, but—
sentences.zh: 过去几个月我们听到了很多关于不确定性的消息，但现在一切都解决了。

sentences.en: We've been hearing a lot about uncertainty over the last few months, but that's all resolved now.
sentences.zh: 过去几个月我们听到了很多关于不确定性的消息，但现在一切都解决了。

sentences.en: So it's all going to get much, much better from here.
sentences.zh: 所以从现在开始，一切都会变得好很多，好很多。

sentences.en: There were plenty of arguments you could make for why they weren't really so terrible.
sentences.zh: 你完全可以列举出很多理由，说明它们其实并没有那么糟糕。

sentences.en: And I think on some basic level, what we're left with here is this economy in stasis where companies aren't really firing workers,
sentences.zh: 我认为从某种基本层面来看，我们现在所处的经济状态是停滞不前的，企业并没有真正解雇员工，

sentences.en: but they're not really hiring them yet either, where, you know, consumers are still spending and sales are still there,
sentences.zh: 但他们也还没有真正开始招聘，你知道，消费者仍在消费，销售额也还在，

sentences.en: but companies are reluctant to make big investments, big bets that that's going to continue going forward.
sentences.zh: 但企业不愿进行大规模投资，不愿押注这种增长势头会持续下去。

sentences.en: Some of that may be because of tariffs.
sentences.zh: 这其中部分原因可能是关税问题。

sentences.en: Some of that may be because of immigration.
sentences.zh: 部分原因可能是移民问题。

sentences.en: Some of that may be because of just sort of the general chaos of the first six months of the year.
sentences.zh: 部分原因可能仅仅是因为今年上半年那种普遍的混乱局面。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: There's clearly some real uncertainty about where the economy goes from here.
sentences.zh: 显然，对于经济未来的走向，确实存在一些真正的不确定性。

sentences.en: But beneath all of the noise, beneath all of the drama, as you put it, from Friday, we have an economy that, based on the numbers, is still relatively OK.
sentences.zh: 但撇开所有的噪音，撇开你所说的周五发生的所有戏剧性事件，根据数据来看，我们的经济状况依然相对良好。

sentences.en: And if we were just talking about the numbers instead of the people responsible for producing them,
sentences.zh: 如果我们只是在谈论数据，而不是谈论那些负责产生数据的人，

sentences.en: Natalie, I'm not sure we would be having this conversation today.
sentences.zh: 娜塔莉，我不确定我们今天还会进行这场对话。

sentences.en: Well, Ben, that said, it was great to have you on the show.
sentences.zh: 好吧，本，话虽如此，很高兴你能来参加节目。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: While Texas are waiting for relief, Republican leaders are redrawing maps to silence voters, hijack our democracy.
sentences.zh: 当德克萨斯州民众等待救援时，共和党领导人却在重新划分选区，试图压制选民，劫持我们的民主。

sentences.en: The Democratic lawmakers who fled Texas on Sunday achieved their goal of preventing a major redesign of congressional maps in the state.
sentences.zh: 周日逃离德克萨斯州的民主党议员们实现了他们的目标，阻止了该州国会选区图的重大重绘。

sentences.en: For now.
sentences.zh: 至少目前是这样。

sentences.en: Without a two-thirds quorum, the Texas legislature could not hold a vote on the new maps, which Republicans hope will flip five seats from Democrats to GOP control.
sentences.zh: 由于没有达到三分之二的法定人数，德克萨斯州立法机构无法就新选区图进行投票，共和党人希望通过此举将五个席位从民主党手中夺回，转为共和党控制。

sentences.en: President Trump had called for the redrawing of the districts in order to lock in Republican control over the House in the next midterm elections.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统曾呼吁重绘选区，以确保共和党在下次中期选举中稳固对众议院的控制权。

sentences.en: But the Texas statehouse speaker said that the vote was just on hold and wouldn't be prevented from going through.
sentences.zh: 但德克萨斯州众议院议长表示，投票只是被搁置，并不会被阻止进行。

sentences.en: I will immediately sign the warrants for the civil arrest of the members who have said they will not be here.
sentences.zh: 我将立即签署逮捕令，对那些声称不会出席的议员进行民事逮捕。

sentences.en: He also issued civil arrest warrants for Democrats who left the state.
sentences.zh: 他还对离开该州的民主党人发出了民事逮捕令。

sentences.en: Governor Greg Abbott of Texas said on Monday that he ordered state law enforcement to detain and return any member who, quote, abandoned their duty to Texans.
sentences.zh: 德克萨斯州州长格雷格·阿博特周一表示，他已下令州执法部门拘留并遣返任何“抛弃了对德州人职责”的议员。

sentences.en: He also threatened to try to remove the missing Democrats from their posts.
sentences.zh: 他还威胁要罢免这些失踪的民主党人的职务。

sentences.en: I believe they have forfeited their seats in the state legislature because they're not doing the job they were elected to do.
sentences.zh: 我相信他们已经丧失了在州立法机构的席位，因为他们没有履行选民赋予他们的职责。

sentences.en: And in what officials are calling the largest environmental settlement ever won by a U.S.
sentences.zh: 在官员们所称的美国各州有史以来达成的最大规模环境和解协议中，

sentences.en: state, three major chemical companies agreed on Monday to pay New Jersey $875 million to settle claims linked to pollution from so-called forever chemicals.
sentences.zh: 三家大型化工公司周一同意向新泽西州支付8.75亿美元，以解决与所谓“永久性化学物质”污染相关的索赔。

sentences.en: There are nearly 15,000 of those chemicals in existence, and they're found in things like nonstick cookware, water-repellent clothing, and stain-resistant carpets.
sentences.zh: 目前世界上存在近15000种此类化学物质，它们存在于不粘锅、防水服装和防污地毯等物品中。

sentences.en: And they've been linked to low birth weight, birth defects, and increased risk of some cancers.
sentences.zh: 它们已被证实与低出生体重、出生缺陷以及某些癌症风险增加有关。

sentences.en: The New Jersey attorney general said the state had some of the highest levels of those chemicals in the country.
sentences.zh: 新泽西州总检察长表示，该州此类化学物质的含量处于全国最高水平之列。

sentences.en: Under the deal, the companies, Chemours, DuPont, and Corteva, have to fund the cleanup of four former industrial sites,
sentences.zh: 根据协议，科慕、杜邦和科迪华这三家公司必须为四个前工业场所的清理工作提供资金，

sentences.en: which were once used to manufacture components for explosives, as well as dyes and refrigerants.
sentences.zh: 这些场所曾被用于制造炸药组件、染料和制冷剂。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Ricky Nowetsky, Claire Tannesketter, and Michael Simon-Johnson.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由瑞奇·诺维茨基、克莱尔·坦内斯凯特和迈克尔·西蒙-约翰逊制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by M.J.
sentences.zh: 由M.J.

sentences.en: Davis-Lynn and Lizzo Balin, with help from Mike Benoit.
sentences.zh: 戴维斯-林恩和利佐·巴林编辑，迈克·贝努瓦提供协助。

sentences.en: Research help by Susan Lee.
sentences.zh: 苏珊·李提供研究协助。

sentences.en: Contains original music by Dan Powell, Marion Lozano, and Rowan Nemisto, and was engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 包含丹·鲍威尔、马里昂·洛扎诺和罗文·内米斯托的原创音乐，由克里斯·伍德进行工程制作。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Landsberg of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由Wonderly的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰兹伯格创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Natalie Kittroweth.
sentences.zh: 我是娜塔莉·基特罗韦斯。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》节目，我们将为您准备节日待客之道。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 敬请收听，获取让客人们宾至如归的小贴士。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是那种需要完全黑暗才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是否会睡到不省人事。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们对光线有什么要求？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们是否有过敏或食物敏感？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 您可以在《纽约时报》应用程序或您喜欢的任何播客平台上收听《Wirecutter秀》。
